designGate.prompt: Before writing code, sketch how you will store resting orders at a price level (and how that preserves time priority), how you will find the best bid/ask quickly, and what you would store at insert time so cancel can find one resting order by id without walking the book. Name the price-level container, the best-price lookup structure, and the cancel index.
requiredElements: price level container named (and how it preserves time priority)
cancel index named (id to resting location)

parts.title: Limit and market orders, price-time priority

hints.text: What do you need to find quickly: the best price on each side, and everything resting at that price in the order it arrived? A market order needs the same two things — it just never has a price bound of its own.

A heap per side gets you the best price; a dict from price to a time-ordered container of orders gets you what to match against once you're at that level. Picture three ask levels: 100 (qty 5), 101 (qty 5), 102 (qty 5) — a buy for 12 at 101 sweeps 100 and 101 in full and stops, never touching 102. A market buy for 12 sweeps 100, 101, and 102 — no price stops it, only running out of resting quantity does.

Two dicts (price -> list of resting orders) plus a min-heap of ask prices and a max-heap of bid prices (negate for max). Match by walking the best level's list front-to-back, partial-filling and popping as you go; rest the leftover at the taker's own price. For a market order, reuse the exact same walk with the price check skipped entirely, and simply never call the rest-the-remainder step afterward — whatever didn't fill is dropped, not queued.

probes: What data structure did you choose for price levels, and why?
Why fill at the resting price and not the incoming order's price?
How would a market order that cannot be fully filled behave at a real venue?

parts.title: Cancel without scanning

hints.text: cancel needs to go straight from an order id to its resting location. What would you need to store at insert time to make that possible?

A dict from order id to (which side, which price) turns cancel into a lookup. But removing it from the level's own container is still O(level size) unless the level itself supports O(1) removal by id. Three levels deep at 100 (a, b, c), cancelling "b" must leave a and c in that same order — a scan-and-splice gets this right too, just not in O(1).

Make each price level a dict (order id -> order) instead of a list — Python dicts preserve insertion order, so time priority is unchanged, but del level[order_id] is now O(1). Pair it with order_id -> (book, price) for the lookup.

probes: cancel in better than scanning the whole book — what's the complexity now, and what did you index at insert time to get there?
What would go wrong if you kept part 1's list-based price level?

parts.title: Amend in place

hints.text: Reducing qty must not change who is in front at that price. What would go wrong if amend were implemented as cancel plus a new submit?

You already have a pointer to the resting record from part 2's index. Shrinking is mutating qty on that record in place. Growing is different — three orders resting at 100 (a:5, b:5, c:5); amending a from 5 to 2 leaves the queue a, b, c; amending a from 5 to 9 must leave the queue b, c, a.

amend looks up the id index, treats 0 as cancel, and otherwise compares new_qty to the resting qty: shrink or no-op sets qty in place (same dict key, same position); grow sets qty then deletes and re-inserts the same key into its level's dict — re-insertion after deletion is what puts it at the back, using the same insertion-order property that gave you O(1) cancel.

probes: Walk through why growing an order in place would steal time priority if it kept its position.
Can a market order be amended or cancelled once submitted? Why or why not?

criteria: price-time priority exact across limit, market, and amend
amend-down keeps FIFO; cancel of a middle-of-level order does too
cancel index introduced without restructuring price levels twice
market reuses limit's matching logic rather than duplicating it
amend mutates the resting record instead of cancel-and-reinsert
heap for best-price lookup, dict for O(1) id-based removal
no full-book scan anywhere past part 1
partial-fill, empty-book, and amend-grow edge cases considered before being told
stated why fills happen at the resting price, what cancel's complexity is, and why amend cannot grow in place without losing priority

provenance.note: Merged from two hand-written pads that turned out to be the same question: order-book (candidate reports of a Jane Street techinterview / intern "craft demo"; Jane Street does not publish this one) and matching-engine (Jump Trading, candidate report). Parts 1 and 2 combine the stronger prompt/test material from each; part 3 (amend) is Jump's, with the grow-in-place behavior changed from raising ValueError to re-queuing behind the level — a real venue lets you grow an order, it just costs you priority.
